articleTitle: Multiple input DC-DC topologies in renewable energy systems - A general review
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE 3rd International Symposium on Exploitation of Renewable Energy Sources (EXPRES)
abstract: The paper reviews the main multi-input converter and systems topologies for power flow control in renewable energy systems, with more than one energy generation unit. The multi-input converters/systems are synthesized from two or more single input converters, which have only one output filter and one control system, coordinated by a common energy management unit. The circuits configurations and theoretical aspects are presented, as a results of the bibliographic analysis.

articleTitle: Optimal energy mix for a grid connected hybrid wind — Photovoltaic generation system
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE 3rd International Symposium on Exploitation of Renewable Energy Sources (EXPRES)
abstract: Taking into account the directives of the European Union concerning the increasing role of renewable power sources for supplying loads and reduction of CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> emission, this paper presents details of the technical and economic characteristics for a hybrid solution generation power system. The goal of this micro power system is to supply residential electrical load that consist in 60 consumers of 5 kW each. Yet, considering the different variability of the most important renewable resources, wind and solar, the hybrid solution is investigated to found the optimal mix solar-wind for a maximum founding option. The investigation is realized using the NREL HOMER package.

articleTitle: COP of heating-cooling system with heat pump
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE 3rd International Symposium on Exploitation of Renewable Energy Sources (EXPRES)
abstract: This paper analyzes the coefficient of performance separately for the heat pump and separately for the heating system-cooling heat pump. Stationary mathematical model with concentrated state parameters has been created. The analysis was done with the mathematical models of coefficient of performance for heat pumps and separately for the heating-cooling system with heat pump. For the analysis, graph-analytical method optimization was applied. The numerical results are presented in graphics.

articleTitle: Advantages of FEM analysis in electrical machines optimization used in wind energy conversion systems
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE 3rd International Symposium on Exploitation of Renewable Energy Sources (EXPRES)
abstract: The present paper refers to some examples that use the finite element method (FEM) in the process of analysis, design and optimization of the electrical machines used in wind energy conversion systems. The 2D-FEM program Opera 13 of Vector Fields is used in the analyzed examples. These examples refer to two types of synchronous generators with permanent magnets. Some possibilities and advantages of electrical machine optimization, using the FEM-programming packages available today, are pointed out in the present paper.

articleTitle: Autoregression test of solar photovoltaic energy generation
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE 3rd International Symposium on Exploitation of Renewable Energy Sources (EXPRES)
abstract: The photovoltaic (PV) generation spreads over the world breezily. The PV cells designed for different conditions are tested in laboratories. One of the key of the PV application is the project economy appraisal that estimates the produced energy. The practical energy generation is disturbed by meteorological events (shower, precipitation, thermal circumstances) that influence the ideal production. In this paper a methodology is shown that through special autoregression method filters the noises and disturbances from the measured energy production curves and makes possible to measure the real "practical" production characteristics of the PV panels. These results help to fit better the DC/AC inverters to the strings and also to make more reasonable investment project plans.

articleTitle: Study of brake transient regimes for a small wind generator
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE 3rd International Symposium on Exploitation of Renewable Energy Sources (EXPRES)
abstract: The paper presents a study for implementing a brake sequence for a small wind generator for regimes that exceeds the rated values. Considering data from a real wind generator, two scenarios are presented: first, during a strong wind gust both the electrical and the mechanical brakes are coupled and, for the second case, a fault in the permanent magnet synchronous generator (PMSG) is caused. This study allows the correct dimensioning of the electric brake load resistors, the setting of the values for the rotation speed at which the different brakes are coupled, in order to respect the structural imposed limits such as maximum current through the PMSG, the maximum torque supported by the wind turbine axis.

articleTitle: Optimized integration of renewable energy
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE 3rd International Symposium on Exploitation of Renewable Energy Sources (EXPRES)
abstract: Decentralized energy and large scale renewables energy is a revolution envisages a development pathway which turns the present energy supply structure into a sustainable system. Optimized integration of renewable energy, in the suburbs and city will produce power and heat as well as consume it. The roofs and facades of public buildings are ideal for harvesting solar energy photovoltaic, solar facade will be decorative element (on office and apartment) buildings. The PV system will more competitive to use them more widely. (Design will be enable architects.) Solar thermal collectors, produce hot water Thermal energy with heat-pumps or thermal water (800 m deep well) integrated in this system, with geothermal heat-and power plant. The wind energy also. It is important to optimize the energy system.

articleTitle: Improvement of biogas production by biotechnological manipulation of the microbial population
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE 3rd International Symposium on Exploitation of Renewable Energy Sources (EXPRES)
abstract: Biogas is a renewable energy carrier and the production of biogas is associated with double benefits: elimination of environmental pollution problems is coupled with the generation of useful energy. Biogas technologies commonly apply natural anaerobic consortia of microbes. This is partly due to the fact that, from a microbiological aspect, this is a very complicated and complex system. Moreover, the population dynamics of the natural ecosystems could not be properly studied before the introduction of molecular biological techniques. Research on the diversity of these microbial communities is needed for the optimization of biogas production technologies as their economic viability is closely related to the efficacy of the concerted microbiological actions. A systematic study, using 5-litre CSTR digesters, disclosed that a key fermentation parameter is the loading rate of organic total solids (OTS) in maintaining an altered population balance.

articleTitle: Power quality monitoring and analysis. Case study for 220/110 kV substation
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE 3rd International Symposium on Exploitation of Renewable Energy Sources (EXPRES)
abstract: Power quality is the set of regulations of electrical properties that allows electrical systems to function without significant loss of performance or aging. The term is used to describe electric power that drives an electrical load and the load's ability to operate properly with that electric power. Without the proper power, an electrical device (or load) may malfunction, fail prematurely or not operate at all. There are many ways when poor quality electric power is recorded and many more causes of such poor quality power. The purpose of the paper is to analyze the impact that different consumers, acting on the open market, has with respect to the power quality aspects. Within the paper a real case study is analyzed. It is represented by a real substation within the Romanian Power System. The power quality monitoring process has been performed in case of the respective substation. The links with the rest of the power system, such as two important hydro power plants and the neighbouring area has been also considered.

articleTitle: The contribution of UFR in measuring water volume by water meter in a single household
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE 3rd International Symposium on Exploitation of Renewable Energy Sources (EXPRES)
abstract: A test rig was set up in the Hydraulic Laboratory of the Faculty of Civil Engineering in Subotica (Republic of Serbia) to model two-outlet water supply systems (consumption was measured by water meters no. 2 and 3), with total flow rate lower than Q<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sub>. According to the applied pressure and flow, the system models the water supply pipeline of a single household. The rated diameter of water meters is 20 mm, manufactured by Potiski vodovodi/Tisa Region Waterworks/ Ltd. Horgos (Republic of Serbia). The characteristic water meter flow rates are: flow activating the water meter propeller (Q<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a</sub>) is between 0,0052 and 0,0067 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>/h, Q<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">min</sub>=0,05 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>/h, Q<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t</sub>=0,2 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>/h and Q<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sub>=2,5 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>/h. Upstream to water meter no. 3 a UFR was installed, manufactured by A.R.I. from Jerusalem (Israel), having a rated diameter of 20 mm, product type T30. Water supply system losses with discharges Q<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub><;Q<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">min</sub> are modelled at water meter no. 3. Water flow at water meter no. 2 was either Q<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>=0 or Q<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">min</sub>≤Q<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>≤Q<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sub>. According to the measurements, the most significant contribution of the UFR in measuring water volume by a water meter of a single household is in the discharge range of Q<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a</sub>, just prior to activation of the water meter propeller: a) 70,47% at flow rates Q<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>=0 and Q<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>=0,005-0,0052 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>/h, and b) 7,47% at flow rates Q<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>=0,0559-0,0577 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>/h and Q<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>=0,0049-0,0050 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>/h respectively.

articleTitle: Energy analysis of geothermal heat pumps with U-tube installations
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE 3rd International Symposium on Exploitation of Renewable Energy Sources (EXPRES)
abstract: Heat pumps can be used for different purposes for building services, including the heating, cooling and domestic hot water production. Heat pumps play the following role with regard to energy: they obtain heat from the environment of lower temperature (e.g. air, water, earth) and transfer it into the building at a higher temperature. In this paper we demonstrate a calculation method to obtain the amount of extractable heat from the earth in the function of time, mass flow and the spacing of U-tube legs. We constructed differential equations for the modelling of U-tube. In these equations the calculation of overall thermal resistance is complex. Much research has been done on this topic so far. In our paper we put forward a method to obtain overall thermal resistance in the function of time and the spacing of U-tube legs. Furthermore, we graphically show the change of the extractable temperature and the value of COP for boreholes with separate diameters.

articleTitle: Resonant Stirling engines
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE 3rd International Symposium on Exploitation of Renewable Energy Sources (EXPRES)
abstract: The paper contains a brief overview of development of the Stirling engine with basic functioning and structure of the division. The second part explains the detailed operation of resonant Stirling engine, with a demonstration of examples of use in practice. The last part refers to the view Lamina Flow Stirling Engine.

articleTitle: Pressure drop during condensation of refrigerant R134a inside horizontal tubes
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE 3rd International Symposium on Exploitation of Renewable Energy Sources (EXPRES)
abstract: The author introduces and analyses the two-phase pressure drop correlation for refrigerant R134a in the condenser of a heat pump heating-cooling system. The following correlation will be included: the Lockhart and Martinelli, Friedel, Chrishom, Tran et al, Wang et al. and the Wilson et al. The previously mentioned correlations were analyzed numerically depending on mass velocity and vapor quality. The aim of the analysis is to choose the optimum model from the tested ones. The applied method of analysis is numeric-graphic.

articleTitle: Respecting the thermodynamics principles of the heat transfer - As the most important condition for achieving high energy efficiency in buildings - Energy of the ground and heat pumps - The most reliable alternative energy source
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE 3rd International Symposium on Exploitation of Renewable Energy Sources (EXPRES)
abstract: The solution of accumulating and keeping the heat in the walls is through insulating from the outside, a common method used in Europe although it hadn't been confirmed on the physical basis, in regards with the conditions of continental climate, may it be in winter or in summer. In effect, during summer season part of the heat gets inside despite the insulations in the walls and over the night the condition within doesn't improve as the insulation would not let it pass through. During winter season, it is unacceptable to sacrifice solar energy when there is still plenty of a sunny day, for the reason that the insulation on the external side of the walls is blocking the sun's energy. From aspects of thermodynamics, the best solution would be to set the insulation on the ceiling and to use walls with optimal thermal insulation thru their entire thickness and at the same time, which are sound- and fireproof as well. This article recommends technical solutions, confirmed by positive feedbacks; StiroFert and a lightweight formwork-insulating concrete blocks, demonstrate and execute a high energy efficiency (energy consumption for heating and cooling of 64 KW/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> on an annual basis). In order that heating and cooling system through the use of heat pumps with downhole heat exchangers and with the coefficient of thermal efficiency of 1:5 to 1:6, it is necessary to implement this solution of transferring the solar energy into the ground around the downhole heat exchangers, so it could be applied not only individually but also in major cities. This technology would not only return the seized energy from the ground but could also bring in the ground a much larger amount of totally free solar energy by transporting through the thermal oil from solar collectors to the ground around the downhole heat exchangers. The leading consumers of energy in the world are buildings. In average, they use 50% of the total produced energy. The consumption would be reduced enormously in up to 15% using the described solution. Thus, the result would be the end of all crises that have befallen the world (energy, ecological, economic), improvement of world economy, social development and prosperity of mankind.

articleTitle: Development of a solar collector for thermal applications
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE 3rd International Symposium on Exploitation of Renewable Energy Sources (EXPRES)
abstract: This article deals with theory and practice of solar collectors for thermal applications. In the first part the theoretical fundamentals are introduced. The second part is about development of a prototype solar collector. The third part introduces testing and test results of a built prototype.

articleTitle: The intelligent energy
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE 3rd International Symposium on Exploitation of Renewable Energy Sources (EXPRES)
abstract: We civilized citizens are accustomed to hot tap water, comfortable temperature in rooms and cooled food at home. These things are part of our everyday life and organic components of our lifestyle. We do not recognize this modern luxury really until they are lost. The issue with our current lifestyle is the growth in consumption which comes with increasing energy prices and growing environmental pollution. Therefore the required usage of more efficient low energy consumption equipment is not enough. There is a need for higher level review of our everyday activities in order to change them. To complete that change more data is needed to be collected, retrieved and stored. The solution for this job can be e.g. the Smart monitoring equipment. This paper gives an overview of the new kind of load management systems. Additionally their field of application, different functions will be discussed. Smart metering is a clever step to a sustainable future.

articleTitle: Thermopile battery, thermoelectric generator as the only possible alternative for future
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE 3rd International Symposium on Exploitation of Renewable Energy Sources (EXPRES)
abstract: Sun supplies the purest energy available on the Earth. Hungary and Serbia seems to be even further from this energy source free from CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> emission, since in spite of the fact that, these states has excellent geographical features neither our present governments non supports this issue to a sufficient extent. A correct purchase price of solar energy should be determined in harmony with the European directives, as nearly all our neighbouring countries have higher achievements in utilising renewable energy sources. Today thermopiles can be found in various applications for temperature or radiation measurements and for electric energy production. It is in the initial stage, especially space technology applications. There exist, for example, surface temperature sensors, gas sensors based on the Lambert-Beer law of absorption, and vacuum sensors. Based on the thermoelectric effect, the thermopile can be used as a heat sensor to measure thermal radiation. A thermopile is made of thermocouple junction pairs connected electrically in series. The absorption of thermal radiation by one of the thermocouple junctions, called the active junction, increases its temperature.

articleTitle: Construction of an innovative geothermal and biomass-based heating plant in Vácrátót
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE 3rd International Symposium on Exploitation of Renewable Energy Sources (EXPRES)
abstract: Hungary begins an intensive development. At present, geothermal heat consumption is about 4.5 PJ a year. This very small energy quantity can be raised to more than 60 PJ a year on the basis of the available energy basis data. Nowadays, geothermal heat has a tiny share in district heat supply in Hungary. In addition to the official district heating, also other utilization in building heating is to be enhanced: at least partial heat supply of self-government or state owned buildings, agricultural and village heating shall be realized in the immediate future.

articleTitle: Power systems expansion considering large wind farms. Case study: Western Romania power system
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE 3rd International Symposium on Exploitation of Renewable Energy Sources (EXPRES)
abstract: The amount of renewable energy sources constantly increased during recent years requiring detailed analysis about their impact on system security and operation. Because of the variability of these sources, which is the main aspect that affects the operating conditions of the power system, new tools of analysis are necessary. This paper presents the analysis of large wind farm integration in nowadays power system using stochastic power flow approach and random contingency analysis. The Western Romania power system is used as a case study.

articleTitle: Present state of sun collectors in Hungary
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE 3rd International Symposium on Exploitation of Renewable Energy Sources (EXPRES)
abstract: The article shows the non-exhaustive theoretical bases of the thermal utilization of solar energy. Based on statistical data it gives an overview of the spread of sun collectors in Hungary. It gives the reasons responsible for the current situation and proposes possible solutions.

articleTitle: Hydrogenerators refurbishment within Romanian power system
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE 3rd International Symposium on Exploitation of Renewable Energy Sources (EXPRES)
abstract: The power quality is one of the main interests within the power generation, delivery and transmission domains. In order to have a higher quality for the power produced in synchronous generators (mainly located in hydro power plants), using an adequate excitation system is essential. This paper shows a general overview of the main tasks which Romanian power producers have to accomplish today. It also presents, several case studies concerning the existing technical solutions (used for the excitation system of synchronous generators) applied in Romania until now. The main goal of this paper is to present the actual situation in this area, to identify some solutions and tendencies concerning the updating of the existing Romanian generators, in order to accomplish all European power standards and regulations. This study has been performed by the authors by taking in consideration opinions coming from the industrial environment.

articleTitle: Towards zero energy buildings: New and retrofitted existing buildings
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE 3rd International Symposium on Exploitation of Renewable Energy Sources (EXPRES)
abstract: Zero energy cities are the realistic future and the final goal concerning energy in the building sector. To achieve such cities, the zero energy buildings have to be defined, concerning conditions to be fulfilled, way of proofing them and to find a procedure how existing buildings to be refurbished and be prepared to join the zero energy cities. It is a long period of work, which also depend of new technology development, standards, national legislation, economic situation. The paper analyses existing definitions, confusing among them, approach to zero energy buildings and the problem of existing buildings which are not efficient and need to be refurbished. The study of refurbishment of existing buildings in Belgrade are also discussed and possible energy achievements are estimated.. This issue occupies researchers, specialists in energy, heating, air conditioning, also entire building industry and of course t architects. Each year there are conferences, seminars and even congresses treating this topic at the fairs and exhibition new result of new technology always brings something new. The January ASHRAE conference had the motto “zero energy buildings,” in India is going to be seminar how to build such buildings, in Autumn, Italian Society will have the similar conference and in the program is also refurbishment of existing buildings as the step to get zero energy buildings. The coming REHVA conference in Spring also has the motto Zero energy houses.

articleTitle: Renewable energy sources and energy efficiency for building's greening: From traditional village houses via high-rise residential building's BPS and RES powered co- and tri-generation towards net ZEBuildings and Cities
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE 3rd International Symposium on Exploitation of Renewable Energy Sources (EXPRES)
abstract: As an introduction to the current approaches to building's greening and sustainability this paper outlines the intrinsic harmony of the traditional village houses encompassing efficiency and balanced use of renewable materials and energy sources. Further paper reviews technical advances in integrating energy efficiency, solar and other renewable energy sources in new and existing buildings, to approach sustainable net Zero Energy Buildings, villages and cities. Paper stresses importance of the BPS (Building Performance Simulation) and Co-simulation in developing reliable method/engineering procedures for RES co-utilization and interwoven "energy mix" scenarios optimization, including existing buildings RES integrated refurbishment. Finally, presented are study results on the technical feasibility of efficient/cost-effective use of relatively low temperature geothermal waters for co-and tri-generation of electricity and heat for heating and/or cooling by absorption refrigeration for building integration. As a result of global warming a need for air conditioning is in extreme growth in Central and Southeastern Europe, as well as in many other regions in the world rich in low temperature geothermal waters <;100°C (<;212°F), and there is a growing interest to utilize these waters in an efficient and cost effective way. It is well known that Kalina thermodynamic cycle can convert relatively low temperature energy, at relatively low temperature difference towards environment, to mechanical power and further to electricity using as a working fluid mixture comprised of at least two different components (water and ammonia). However, its co-generation efficiency at the heat source temperatures below and about 100°C is too low. That was the reason to explore technical possibilities to expand the low-temperature Kalina cycle's geo-water utilization for co-and tri-generation based on the co-utilization hybridization of geothermal with solar or other renewable energy sources (RES).

articleTitle: Impact of large-scale implementation of photovoltaic devices to CO2 emissions
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE 3rd International Symposium on Exploitation of Renewable Energy Sources (EXPRES)
abstract: Our civilization faces growing prospects of climate problems. They are blamed to current consumption of fossil fuels (FF) for electricity generation in FF plants. This yields to massive CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> release into atmosphere and environment pollution, increase in average temperature of earth and climate problems. One way to prevent this is to use photovoltaic (PV) devices instead of FF plants for electricity generation. To replace some of FF plants, one may erect PV devices. However, this uses existing electrical energy for their construction. In this research, theoretical approach is developed to calculate the yearly energy consumption and the yearly CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> emission during implementation of the PV devices. Then, the impact of large-scale implementation of PVs to increase and decrease in CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> emissions is studied. It is found out that there may exist an immediate high increase in CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> emissions and after that its decrease. The magnitude of this decrease depends on CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> payback time (TCP) for introduced PV device. Lower TCP yields very low CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> emission for the energy system, while higher TCP may increase CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> emission of the energy system within its life time.

articleTitle: About the Serbian energy problems
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE 3rd International Symposium on Exploitation of Renewable Energy Sources (EXPRES)
abstract: This paper analyzes energy efficiency in Serbia. Regardless of constant attempts to improve and increase energy efficiency and to expand utilization of renewable energy sources, it seems that accomplished results are still very modest. The analysis of several energy indicators and their changes in the midterm period, confirms this statement. The paper also provides views for necessary actions which can contribute to the significant growth of energy efficiency in Serbia.
